officialName.value: Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv
officialName.note: Search-snippet lead (official domain, 2026-10-12) — NOT verified; read the official page before publishing. Snippets: an older official admission-policy page on knu.ua (URL suggests 2013) reads "Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv provides training for foreigners in Ukrainian, Russian or English languages (at student's option)", and a result on pdis.knu.ua is titled "Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv". The Ukrainian name Київський національний університет імені Тараса Шевченка appeared only on THIRD-PARTY admissions-aggregator cards (vstup.osvita.ua). Medical teaching sits in the university's Educational and Scientific Center "Institute of Biology and Medicine" (title of the official page knu.ua/en/departments/bm/; Ukrainian title on biomed.knu.ua: НАВЧАЛЬНО-НАУКОВИЙ ЦЕНТР "ІНСТИТУТ БІОЛОГІЇ ТА МЕДИЦИНИ"), a faculty-level unit of the university and not a separate university; the same Ukrainian unit name, ННЦ "Інститут біології та медицини", appears under the university on the 2018 EDEBO admission portal (government) and on the third-party cards. Two first-round wordings ("Kyiv National University Department of Medicine" and a wording from a Karazin University news title) were not reproduced on re-check and are not recorded. The results do not state the university's ownership or legal form. Confirm the full official name, in English and Ukrainian, on the official homepage.

overview: Research draft record, unpublished: every statement below is an unverified lead, not a verified fact. A classical university in Kyiv, Ukraine, whose Educational and Scientific Center "Institute of Biology and Medicine" (a unit of the university, not a separate university) hosts the six-year Medicine programme (specialty 222); an undated official page for foreign citizens lists it as taught in English. Draft record built from search-snippet leads on 2026-10-12. The official university pages behind the Medicine leads are undated or date from 2013 to 2020, and no dated statement on teaching format was found, so whether, where and how foreign students are taught in 2026–27 is an open question. No fee, deadline or intake date is recorded. Every field below is awaiting verification against the official pages listed under research references and nothing here is presented as a current fact.

accreditation.note: Record accreditation only from a NAQA register entry or the official certificate. Nothing recorded. Kept strictly separate: (1) State registration (EDEBO): the current EDEBO register record for the university was not seen in the search results (the register host was also refused at the build environment's proxy); not evidence either way. A dated EDEBO admission-portal offer (vstup2018.edbo.gov.ua, government, search-tool paraphrase) lists a full-time Master's, (222) Medicine, at ННЦ "Інститут біології та медицини" under the university for the 2018 intake — an old admission offer, not a register entry and not evidence of current admissions. (2) Programme licence: no licence document or current EDEBO licence record seen. Leads only: the 2018 admission offer gave a licensed capacity of 100 and 10 state-funded places for that intake (dated 2018, not a current licence); the undated knu.ua foreign-citizens table gives "201 places" / "licensed intake of 201" for Medicine in English, and whether that is a licensed volume or an actual intake is uncertain. (3) National programme accreditation (NAQA): no NAQA accreditation decision or certificate for the Medicine (222) programme found; a NAQA expert report uploaded 2025/10 concerns the university's Biology programme, not Medicine, and a NAQA self-assessment PDF for the university (2025/10) showed only facility-area data. (4) International accreditation: none found in the results (no WFME-aligned accreditation was found; not evidence of absence). An international accreditation is neither NAQA accreditation nor recognition. (5) The Ministry of Education's higher-education standard for 222 Medicine at master's level (Order No. 1197 of 08.11.2021) is said, unverified, to name the Institute among the institutions involved (role not shown); a standard is neither a licence nor an accreditation.

recognition.note: Recognition is decided separately by each destination country's regulator (for example India's National Medical Commission). Record it only from a tier-4 page on a recognition-authority host the owner has listed (N24 b; none listed yet), quoting what that page says, with its date. A World Directory of Medical Schools (WDOMS) listing is a directory entry, not recognition; a university's own claim of WHO, NMC or ECFMG recognition is not recognition; an international accreditation is not recognition; institutional registration (EDEBO), the programme licence and programme accreditation (NAQA) are separate claims. Claim seen, not recorded: a first-round search summary said the English-language Master's in Medicine leads to a diploma "that the university says is recognized in the EU" (biomed.knu.ua, search-tool paraphrase); the re-check did not search for it, so it is not reproduced, and in any case it is the university's own claim, not recognition by any regulator. No destination-regulator source was found. No WDOMS entry appeared in the results (access limitation, not evidence of absence). Never imply a right to practise in any country.

level.note: Search-snippet lead (government domain, 2026-10-12) — NOT verified; read the official page before publishing. The knu.ua foreign-citizens table that lists Medicine sits under a "bachelor" URL and does not state the level, and the first-round biomed.knu.ua "Master's Programme in Medicine" quote was not reproduced on re-check. Whether the university classifies it as a single-cycle (integrated) master's, and the level for foreign applicants, must be read on the programme page.
